title: End each reading by using its meaning
statement: End each reading with a task that does something with the meaning, such as applying it, critiquing it or taking a position, not only with answering items.
detail: A reading quality canon of 518 rules makes it one of its 13 priority-one rules that each reading ends in a task that does something with the meaning: apply it, critique it, make or solve something, or take a position, not only answer items. Its reason is that comprehension is not finished until the reader has done something with what was understood. Applied to a grade 5 lesson, the canon notes that the bar rises there to taking a position, critiquing and applying.

evidence.quote: Each reading ends in a task that *does something* with the meaning — apply it, critique it, make/solve something, take a position — not only answer items ("comprehension is not finished until the reader has done something with what was understood").
the 518-rule canon per `MANIFEST.json`: 13 priority-1 + 505 priority-2 rules
The reading should end in doing something with the meaning; at G5 the bar rises (take a position, critique, apply).
